title: Client interop guidelines for zero-downtime updates: pagination, retries, and streaming
creator: Priya Nair
description: PRD defining requirements and acceptance criteria for Python/TS/Go clients to ensure predictable pagination semantics, idempotent retries, streaming API behavior, and a backward-compatible upgrade path that enables zero-downtime updates for customer applications.
background: Multiple internal and customer reports show subtle incompatibilities across SDK versions when we change pagination cursors, alter default retry behavior, or modify streaming envelope framing. These have led to integration regressions and increased support churn. We want a single set of product and API-level requirements that SDK owners can implement to avoid breaking customers during runtime upgrades and to enable safe, staged platform changes.
problem_statement: Changes to API responses or client defaults (cursor format, opaque page tokens, retry windows, streaming chunk/event framing) have caused live client breakage during server-side rollouts. There is no unified contract documenting tolerances, deprecation windows, or explicit compatibility tests for SDKs in Python, TypeScript, and Go.
solution_outline: Define a minimal compatibility contract: stable pagination token form (opaque string), explicit pagination headers, retry idempotency markers and default retry policy boundaries, streaming envelope backwards-compatible additions, and a standard deprecation + rollout cadence. Provide automated cross-language compatibility tests, CI gates, and SDK guidance docs + code snippets for safe client upgrades.
out_of_scope: Full SDK refactors unrelated to compatibility (UI-only changes)
requirements: Pagination: page tokens must remain opaque strings. Server may add new token versions but must decode both new and legacy tokens for at least 180 days after rollout.
Pagination: responses must include explicit metadata fields 'next_page_token' and 'total_estimate' when available; clients must treat missing 'total_estimate' as unknown, not zero.
Pagination: SDK helpers should expose both cursor-based and offset-style convenience APIs, with clear mapping documented in each client guide.
Retries: define a standard idempotency key header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' for operations where safe retries are expected; SDKs should automatically surface an idempotency param for relevant calls.

Retries: default SDK retry policy: (a) 3 attempts total, (b) exponential backoff base 200ms capped at 3s, (c) retry on 5xx, 429 (with Retry-After honored), and network errors only. Any change to the default must be behind a major version bump and documented in the changelog.

Streaming: streaming API frames must be forward-compatible: servers may add optional envelope fields but must never remove required fields. SDKs must ignore unrecognized envelope keys and pass through raw payload as fallback.
Streaming: provide a 'streaming-mode' negotiation header so client and server can agree on framing v1/v2. Default should negotiate v1 unless explicitly opted-in by client.
Compatibility tests: integrate cross-SDK tests that exercise pagination token upgrades, retry idempotency, and streaming envelope evolution in the Redwood CI matrix.
Deprecation windows: breaking or protocol-level changes require a minimum of 90 days notice, a migration guide, and server-side tolerant handling for at least 180 days prior to enforcement.
SDK docs: publish language-specific quickstarts that show safe upgrade patterns, how to enable legacy behaviors, and migration recipes for each breaking change scenario.
scope_changes: Initial scope included only pagination and retries; streaming compatibility was added after engineering feedback (2026-03-05).
Added requirement to provide CI compatibility tests across all three SDKs following PM/Eng sync (2026-03-08).
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize contract and acceptance criteria; publish PRD and RFC in Confluence; solicit feedback from SDK owners (PM, Eng, DX).
Week 1-2: Implement server-side token tolerant layer and streaming negotiation header behind feature flags; add compatibility tests to CI; create SDK task templates.
Week 3-6: SDK teams (Python/TS/Go) implement helpers, docs, and CI gates. Run cross-SDK compatibility matrix nightly.
Week 7: Ramp feature flag on small percentage (5-10%) of traffic; monitor errors and regressions via dashboards.
Week 8-12: Widen rollout to 50% then 100%; maintain tolerant decoding for 180 days post-100% before removing legacy paths.
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts both legacy and vN pagination tokens for at least 180 days after deployment; automated tests prove dual-token acceptance.
SDK default retry behavior matches policy in requirements and is configurable; test harness verifies expected number of attempts for simulated 500 and 429 responses.
Streaming negotiation header works: clients default to v1; opt-in to v2 succeeds; unrecognized envelope fields are ignored and do not crash clients in all three languages.
Cross-language CI matrix passes for pagination, retries, and streaming tests for five consecutive nightly runs before GA.
Migration docs and quickstarts for Python/TS/Go published in the SDK repo README and linked from developer docs.
No customer-facing incidents attributable to the rollout during the 12-week rollout window (tracked in support dashboard).
Telemetry: error-rate delta for affected endpoints remains within 0.2% of baseline during rollout; latency impact <10% p95 increase.
metrics_success: Compatibility CI pass rate: 100% for required tests across SDKs for 5 consecutive nights.
Support ticket reduction: within 3 months post-rollout, related integration regression tickets decrease by >=60%.
Service error delta: p50/p95 token decode errors reduced to 0 after tolerant layer is live.
